title: Fleet Queue Jockey: Interactive scaling dashboard and change journal for Dedicated fleets
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a unified Console surface — nicknamed 'Fleet Queue Jockey' — that lets operators (SREs, platform engineers) inspect queue/backlog behavior, adjust fleet scaling controls in real time, and review a compact change journal for throughput guarantees and autoscaling policy changes. The feature aims to reduce manual capacity adjustments, shorten incident troubleshoot cycles, and make scaling provenance auditable for postmortems and compliance.
background: Customers on Dedicated capacity repeatedly ask for a single place to correlate sudden latency/backlog spikes with recent autoscale rule edits or operator overrides. Current tooling scatters metrics across dashboards and audit logs are noisy. Teams waste time triangulating Prometheus graphs, recent policy edits, and who performed a manual capacity bump. This feature consolidates these signals and exposes safe, reversible controls.
user_stories: As a platform operator, I want to see per-fleet queue length, pending requests, and effective concurrency so I can decide whether to change autoscale targets.
As an SRE oncall, I want to temporarily bump throughput and have an automatic rollback so I can mitigate a latency incident without leaving a persistent config change.
As a compliance auditor, I want a compact change journal that shows who changed scaling policies and why, linked to a runbook or incident, so audits are easier.
scope_in: Interactive dashboard panel in Console for Dedicated fleets with time-aligned charts: queue depth, request latency P50/P95/P99, current active workers, effective qps
Operator controls: transient throughput override (duration + reason), soft priority bump, and save-to-policy action
Change journal: compact list of policy edits and operator overrides with links to PR/incident IDs and ability to annotate
Integrations: surface links to existing telemetry (Traces/Prometheus/Grafana) and to audit log entries
scope_out: Full redesign of fleet orchestration engine (only UI + small control-plane APIs)
New autoscale algorithms (we will launch with existing rule types and a 'rollback-after' guard)
On-prem air-gapped installation work beyond control-plane API contract
success_metrics: Reduce mean time to mitigation for Dedicated capacity incidents from detection->mitigation by 35% within 3 months
>40% of operator capacity adjustments performed via Console panel (vs. manual infra changes) within 6 weeks of GA
Audit noise reduction: 60% fewer cross-referenced logs required per postmortem (tracked via internal postmortem checklist)
engineering_notes: Will require a lightweight control-plane endpoint to apply transient throughput overrides: POST /fleets/{id}/overrides
Backend must emit a canonical change-event (change_id) written to audit log store and returned to UI for journaling
Performance: dashboard queries should use pre-aggregated telemetry where possible to avoid UI query timeouts during incidents
Ensure RBAC checks: only users with fleet.operator or fleet.admin roles can apply overrides
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard renders for Dedicated fleets and shows time-aligned queue-depth + latency + worker-count charts for the last 60m by default
Operator can apply a transient throughput override with duration (15m/1h/4h/custom) and a required reason; API returns change_id
Change journal lists overrides and policy edits with timestamp, actor, reason, and link to change_id; clicking an entry surfaces the delta and option to annotate
All override actions are recorded in the audit log and visible via existing audit retention policies
RBAC prevents non-privileged users from applying changes and hides controls for read-only roles
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal rollout to SRE and Platform teams (2 weeks) — validate workflow and audit entries
Beta: opt-in for 10 early customer accounts with Dedicated fleets (4 weeks) — gather feedback on UI affordances and rollback behavior
GA: gradual rollout behind feature flag for all Dedicated customers (2 weeks) — monitor usage and any unexpected autoscale interactions
risks: Operators may overuse transient overrides and create oscillation — mitigations: soft rate limits, cooldowns, and mandatory reason with automatic expiration
Change journal could become noisy if we ingest low-value events — mitigation: linting rules and event deduplication in the control plane
Telemetry alignment: chart sync issues across time windows could mislead operators — mitigation: central timebase and server-side alignment
tradeoffs: We prioritize a compact, curated journal instead of shipping raw audit streams to keep the UX digestible; this may omit low-level events initially
Transient overrides are implemented at the control-plane level (fast to ship) rather than deep orchestration changes (slower but more robust)
open_questions: Should overrides be cancellable by other operators or only the actor who created them? (security vs. ops flexibility)
What is the retention period for change journal entries in the Console UI vs. the audit backend?
Do we expose a 'suggested scale' computed by a lightweight heuristic in the first iteration?
